topics.topic: Required behavior for callers racing with lock-file creation and initialization
questions: When another process observes a newly created lock file before its creator has finished applying `LOCK_FILE_MODE`, must it retry until initialization completes, use the provisional file as it stands, or refuse with `state_unavailable`?

When two callers concurrently find no lock file and one caller's exclusive creation makes the other's creation fail because the entry now exists, must the losing caller open and lock the new existing file, retry, or answer `state_unavailable`?

quotes: Creates the project lock file on first use with the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE`, and the missing folders below the state folder with `STATE_FOLDER_MODE`; a missing state folder is refused like a lock file that cannot be opened. It creates an absent lock file in place with the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE`, opens an existing one as it stands without changing it, never follows a link, and holds an operating system lock.

`state_unavailable` when the state folder is missing, when a folder leading to the lock file cannot be created or given its mode or is a symbolic link or not a folder, when the lock file cannot be created, opened, given its mode on creation or locked, or when its entry is a symbolic link or not a regular file.

The lock file is created on
   first use and never removed. It is not written through a temporary name: it is created in place,
   exclusively, for reading and writing and without following a link, and once it is found to be a regular
   file it is given the mode of the imported `LOCK_FILE_MODE` constant, whatever the umask; a failure to
   set that mode is refused like a lock file that cannot be opened. When it already exists it is opened
   for reading and writing without following a link and used as it stands: its mode and its bytes are
   never changed or read, so taking the lock writes nothing.

- INV-12: concurrent placements of one source, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed` and leave one placement record and one stored image (`test_separate_processes_leave_one_placement`), and marks of two `photo_id` values, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other, and leave one mark record holding the `photo_id` whose call answered `marked` (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).
judgement.divergence: A losing concurrent creator retries or waits until the newly created lock file has its final mode and then completes normally, versus treating the provisional file's open failure or the exclusive-create collision as `state_unavailable`; the losing caller observes `replayed` or another normal result in the first behavior and a refusal in the second.
judgement.why: The texts require successful concurrent outcomes but do not define how a caller encountering the creation-and-mode-setting window distinguishes transient initialization from a genuine open or creation failure.

witness.initial: The state folder exists, the project lock file is absent, and the process umask can initially remove permissions that `LOCK_FILE_MODE` will restore.
events: Process A and process B call delivery for the same project and source in separate processes.
Process A creates the lock file exclusively but has not yet applied `LOCK_FILE_MODE`.
Process B's exclusive creation finds the new entry and follows the existing-file path before process A finishes setting its mode.
outcomes: Process B retries or waits for initialization, acquires the lock after process A, and answers `replayed`.
Process B treats the creation collision or provisional open failure as `state_unavailable`.
basis: - INV-12: concurrent placements of one source, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `placed` and otherwise `replayed` and leave one placement record and one stored image (`test_separate_processes_leave_one_placement`), and marks of two `photo_id` values, in one process and in separate processes, answer one `marked`, `replayed` for the same value and `publication_conflict` for the other, and leave one mark record holding the `photo_id` whose call answered `marked` (`test_concurrent_calls_leave_one_placement_and_one_mark`, `test_separate_processes_leave_one_mark`).
It creates an absent lock file in place with the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE`, opens an existing one as it stands without changing it, never follows a link, and holds an operating system lock.

`state_unavailable` when the state folder is missing, when a folder leading to the lock file cannot be created or given its mode or is a symbolic link or not a folder, when the lock file cannot be created, opened, given its mode on creation or locked, or when its entry is a symbolic link or not a regular file.

topics.topic: Classification of missing, non-directory, and dangling-link state-folder path components
questions: Does “a folder on its address does not exist” mean only an actually absent path component, or also a component occupied by a non-folder or a dangling symbolic link, and must those latter cases return absence or `state_unavailable`?

quotes:
A record is absent only when no entry exists at its address, also when a folder on its address does
   not exist; reading a record creates nothing.

A record that is a link, even a dangling one, or that
   cannot be opened or read, is not valid JSON, fails that validation or names another project or source
   is never taken for an absent record: the operation is refused with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode, whose value is
   `state_unavailable`, and changes no record and no stored image.
judgement.why: Only an absent component makes the record absent; a non-folder or dangling-link component prevents the record from being opened and therefore produces `state_unavailable`.

topics.topic: Scope of the prohibition on following symbolic links
questions: Does “never follows a link” apply to the configured state-folder path, contradicting A6 rule 2’s requirement that the state folder is reached “also through a link,” or only to entries below that folder and the lock file itself?

quotes: Creates the project lock file on first use with the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE`, and the missing folders below the state folder with `STATE_FOLDER_MODE`; a missing state folder is refused like a lock file that cannot be opened. It creates an absent lock file in place with the mode of `LOCK_FILE_MODE`, opens an existing one as it stands without changing it, never follows a link, and holds an operating system lock.

Each of them is the installation's own folder and is reached as its
   configured path stands, also through a link; only the entries below it are checked as this rule says.
judgement.why: The public operation unqualifiedly says that it never follows a link, while A6 expressly requires the configured state-folder path to be reached through a link when configured that way.
